Icon on glass, ”Jesus Christ, King and Great High Priest, flanked by archangels”. Model: workshop in Țara Bârsei, second half of the 19th century
DESCRIPTION
Pen-and-ink drawing on glass, fixed with varnish. Painting: tempera, egg emulsion and linseed oil; final protective layer (on the back): oil colours and linseed oil. The icon is painted on glass, 21 x 29 cm. Stained fir frame.
DETAILS
The icon is painted “in mirror image” (partly reconstructed) after a model from Țara Bârsei, second half of the 19th century.
The icon is not available; it will be painted to order.

Why Christ is High Priest, Teacher and King (source: “40 Orthodox theses about God and the salvation of man” – the newspaper Răsunetul)
Jesus Christ is the supreme Teacher or Prophet by His very Person; as a Teacher He is not like any other man, and as a Prophet He surpasses all who came before Him, because He stands on another plane. His teaching is unique, because He is unique, and He is one with His teaching, which springs from Him. “Learn from Me, for I am meek and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.”
Jesus Christ is the supreme prophecy and the culminating revelation, and here we find what is to be known about God and man in all its fullness. The word of Jesus Christ is the living truth and is identical with His Person, for He became the hypostasis of the human spirit. The Person of Jesus Christ and the Kingdom of God that He preaches, preaching Himself, are an absolute and final newness; here lies the infinity of life, this Kingdom of God being the one and only chance of eternal life.
Jesus Christ speaks to people as God, and also as man. He communicates to them the Word of God, but He also communicates His answer as man to God, for He prays for them and teaches them to pray. His teaching calls us to answer Him, while at the same time it glorifies God. As High Priest, Jesus Christ offers Himself as a sacrifice, and this ministry is directed straight to God the Father, but it is also directed towards us, because He wishes to include us in it. Jesus Christ offers as a sacrifice the human nature He took on, so this high-priestly ministry also has its effect on the human nature He assumed. Christ's sacrifice was made for the restoration of human nature in Him, for the deification of this nature in Him. Christ's sacrifice restores communion between God and man. That is why Jesus Christ is always in a state of sacrifice, giving Himself wholly to the Father while at the same time having compassion on us. That is why He is the supreme High Priest, because He is also God; that is why Christ intercedes for us with the Father. Man wishes to enter into communion with God, and God accepts him because man wishes and strives not to sin any more; so God's acceptance comes not because man suffers a punishment for his sin, but, as I said before, because of his sincere efforts to leave the realm of sin.
Jesus Christ is King, and the Saviour is raised to this full royal power through His Resurrection, His Ascension and His sitting at the right hand of the Father, from where He guides the work of salvation and from where He will come in great glory to judge the world. The Saviour's Resurrection shows and proves that history is destined to be raised to another plane, higher than its present one: the plane of incorruptible life, where there is no death, where the freedom of the human spirit, through the Holy Spirit, makes the body transparent.
87830aa78805:
The Entry into Jerusalem – icon painted on glass
An authentic, framed, traditional Romanian icon, made in the style of the icons painted by the Transylvanian icon painters of the 18th–19th centuries, respecting the techniques of this art form. Model: Arpașu de Sus, Țara Oltului, 1872 (Savu Moga)
Painted on glass in several layers, using tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model.
The ink drawing is fixed and protected with varnish, and the finished painting has a protective layer of colour with linseed oil.
The stained fir frame is also handmade.
Icon size: 30x43 cm (without frame); 37x50 cm (with frame)

The theme of this icon is "The Entry of the Lord into Jerusalem", also known as "Palm Sunday".

The Entry of the Lord into Jerusalem, also known as Palm Sunday, is one of the Great Feasts of the Orthodox Church, celebrated on the Sunday before Easter.

A few days before His crucifixion, the Lord Jesus Christ was welcomed, as the Messiah and King of Israel, by the crowds who glorified and honoured Him as He entered Jerusalem riding on the foal of a donkey. In their joy, the crowds threw palm or fig leaves before Him, the symbol of victory, and even the children cried out words of praise to Him.

Traditions
Orthodox Christians celebrate this day as a joyful one, but with the understanding that the days that follow are days of sorrow.

Orthodox Christians in countries where palms and figs do not grow, such as the Romanians or the Russians, use willow branches instead for this feast. The faithful bring to church these branches of willow, fig or palm (also called, by an older name, “stâlpări”, hence the Romanian name of the feast, “Duminica Stâlpărilor”), recalling those with which the Saviour was welcomed as He entered Jerusalem. At the end of the Holy Liturgy, the priest says a prayer of blessing over them, sprinkles them with holy water to sanctify them, and then gives them to the faithful, who adorn their icons with them and keep them with care. In some Churches it is the custom, after the Liturgy, to give out small crosses made of palm leaves, which are then placed by the icons.

On the eve of the feast, in some places a pilgrimage or procession is held, which always starts from one church and ends at (another) church. In this way the people's going out to meet the Lord on His way to Jerusalem is remembered, and the pilgrimage itself also serves to bless the place.

1868fd7fd732:
Sometimes we are blessed with miracles that come into our lives suddenly, like gifts from the Divine, who smiles on us indulgently as we stand amazed...

Not many miracles have happened in my life; there have been few, but they were overwhelming! The most recent one happened almost 3 years ago, on the day of the Annunciation, a holy day on which I began to paint icons on glass.

I didn't know much about the icons painted on glass by our wonderful Transylvanian peasants, about their soul, about their technique, unique in the world, of painting religious scenes in vivid colours, with oversized decorations and in images that blended their real lives with biblical scenes... And I had never painted until that day!

It was the beginning! Since then I have painted almost 80 icons, which are now mostly in private collections of public figures and ordinary people (all of them remarkable people), and in a few churches and monasteries in Romania.

I thank the Lord for this miracle in my life and for giving an extraordinary meaning to the rest of my life!

In painting on glass, it can be said that this type of composition (the theme of the Sorrowful Mother of God) was born in Transylvania. This theme is (in fact) the most frequent in Transylvanian iconography.

The version that became classic throughout Transylvania is the one in which the Mother of God stands with her hands joined in prayer, looking towards the cross of the crucifixion, painted in miniature in the background.
One of the versions of this theme (and one of the most beautiful) was painted in Arpașu de Jos in 1877; after its model I painted the icon whose photos you see here: an authentic, framed, traditional Romanian icon, made in the style of the icons painted by the Transylvanian icon painters of the 18th–19th centuries, respecting the techniques of this art form.

Painted on glass in several layers, using tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model. The ink drawing is fixed and protected with varnish, and the finished painting has a protective layer. The stained fir frame is also handmade.

Size: 21x29 cm (without frame); 27.55x35.5 cm (with frame).

The icon is available to order.
92c095c1497a:
The icon "Jesus – the True Vine", also known as "the Eucharistic Christ", is unique in the world. A beauty that came from the hands of anonymous makers, simple peasants (from a Transylvania under foreign rule), who through their icons painted on glass upheld Orthodoxy with an immense faith in God and in His Works. The icon on this theme is considered to be the Orthodox Romanians' answer to the Calvinist question. They generally painted it in a naive manner, charmingly balanced by the native artistic sense of these Transylvanian peasants! It was made exclusively on glass, in most of the renowned schools of Transylvania: Nicula, Șcheii Brașovului, Gherla, Maierii (Alba Iulia), Lancrăm, Făgăraș, Mărginimea Sibiului.
 Specialists say that ~the icon is a depiction of the Lord's words recorded by John in his Gospel: “I am the true vine...”, and it is found above all in the altar area, at the table of oblation, where the bread and wine are prepared for communion. The vine pouring out of Jesus's body refers to the moment when the wine is changed into the Blood of the Lord during the Holy Liturgy.~
 I have painted this theme, "Jesus – the True Vine", in two versions. One of them (painted after a model from Șcheii Brașovului) is at the top of clients' requests, so I have painted it very many times, but always with the same joy. The second version (painted after a Nicula model) is the icon I am showing you today.
